next_question: On a credential-free substrate, can an independently justified end-to-end product-economics counter (measured per-operation cost such as model calls/tokens, browser/network work, retrieval, verification and repair, rather than the preregistered abstract equal-weight {http_requests, retrieval_calls, verification_calls, repair_attempts} counter) be constructed and measured so that reuse-based localized repair is or is not strictly cheaper than cold re-derivation at L=2 and L=3 - i.e. is the observed counter-dependence a genuine product-economics boundary, or an artifact of an equal-weight counter no external agent actually uses, and therefore should localized repair be permanently dropped from the C-PRODUCT-ECON product story?
